And if you are using AAD Pod Identity, you are running a component that reached end of support in September 2023. Azure Workload Identity replaces both. articles.title: I built Kule: AI agents work on a copy of your folder, and you decide what comes back
articles.summary: Hi, I'm Selçuk. I've been building an open-source tool called Kule, and its first preview release is out. I'd like to tell you what it does, why I built it, and what it can't do yet. The short version: Kule is a control room for AI agents that work on your folders. You point an agent (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, or any agent that speaks ACP) at a folder. Kule gives it a copy-on-write copy of that folder inside a sandbox, looks at what every command really changed, and lets nothing reach the real folder until a policy, or you, says so. Every commit can be undone. ("Kule" means tower in Turkish. Think control tower.) The problem I kept running into Coding agents are good now, good enough that we let them run commands. When an agent runs a command, it runs as you: your files, your ~/.ssh and ~/.aws, your ~/.zshrc, your network, your API keys. What AIPass is AIPass is a framework for Claude Code. It turns single Claude Code sessions into a team of agents that persist. Each agent is a directory on your disk holding, among other things, an identity file, memory files it reads every time it wakes, a mailbox, and standing instructions that hooks inject into every session. When a session ends, the agent does not. The next session starts by reading what the last one wrote. All the agents work on the same filesystem as you, with no per-agent sandbox or worktree.
